analysis.title: The Commodities Feed: US midterm elections key for oil market
key_insights: Oil market is nervous ahead of the US midterm elections. The market is increasingly pricing in the risk of escalation in the Persian Gulf after the elections, but there is still some hope for diplomacy.
ICE Brent settled almost 2.4% higher on Friday to close above $113/bbl. The Dec-26 contract settled at $117.64/bbl on its expiry day.

Vessel attacks have increased in recent weeks, while signs point to more traffic flowing through the Strait of Hormuz. Fears remain high over potential new US and Israeli strikes on Iran after the midterms.
Reports that President Trump wants to give diplomacy a chance weighed on prices in early trading. Iranian negotiators held talks with Qatari mediators in Doha over the weekend, with no result yet.

If the midterms pass with neither strikes nor a deal, the question is whether the geopolitical risk premium persists or unwinds. Many key developments in this conflict have come over weekends, so the market may wait until the end of the week.

Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries resumed late last week after a roughly 2-week pause. During the pause the ICE gasoil crack fell below $70/bbl, its lowest since early October. Further attacks would likely put a floor under the crack.
Russia's deputy prime minister said Russia plans to export 2.15m tonnes of diesel in November, up from a little more than 500kt in October.
OPEC+ kept December output targets unchanged. Most members are producing well below target because of Persian Gulf disruptions.

Speculators added 3,576 lots to the ICE Brent net long, taking it to 245,457 lots as of last Tuesday, driven by fresh longs. This is well below the year-to-date high of about 430k lots in March. ING says a strong catalyst would be needed for more buying, since risk-reward at current prices does not favor adding long risk.

TTF settled more than 6% higher on Friday near EUR104/MWh. Colder-than-usual NW Europe weather could cause large storage draws. EU gas storage peaked just under 75% last Tuesday and is edging lower. ING expects high volatility through the winter.

Gold fell 3.65% to $3,874.62/oz, a one-year low, as higher oil prices raised inflation concerns and expectations that rates stay higher for longer. A tech sell-off added pressure. Energy prices, rate expectations and broader liquidation remain headwinds.
Silver fell more than 6%, extending its October decline to roughly 18%. The widening gold-silver ratio points to gold outperforming silver in the correction.

Copper fell with the risk-off mood, but physical tightness persists. The LME cash-to-three-month backwardation narrowed by almost $48/t to $174.85/t, and the Yangshan premium rose above $200/t. ING sees this as a floor under prices, with possible resistance from price-sensitive demand at elevated levels.

CBOT corn fell nearly 11% in October, the largest monthly decline since June 2023, on harvest supply, weaker export demand and easing Black Sea concerns. 60% of the US corn crop was harvested as of 25 October versus 44% a week earlier.

Speculators cut net long corn by 90,314 lots for a sixth straight week to 55,314 lots. Money managers raised net short CBOT wheat by 23,725 lots to 74,859 lots, and cut net long soybeans by 21,536 lots to 185,400 lots.

sector_views.rationale: Oil is pricing a geopolitical risk premium ahead of the US midterms, with the direction depending on whether strikes or a deal follow. Speculative length is well below the March high, but ING sees limited risk-reward for adding longs at current prices.
Higher energy prices, higher-for-longer rate expectations and broader liquidation are headwinds for gold and silver. Gold is outperforming silver.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Brent rose almost 2.4% on the day as markets priced in the risk of Persian Gulf escalation.
The expiring contract settled above the front-month level.
Gas rose more than 6% on colder weather forecasts and falling storage.
A one-year low, down 3.65% on inflation concerns and higher-for-longer rate expectations.
Storage is edging lower as the heating season starts.
Narrowed by almost $48/t but still elevated, which signals tight physical supply.

tension_points.bull_case: Fears of fresh US and Israeli strikes on Iran after the midterms, vessel attacks, and a speculative net long still well below the March high leave room for speculators to add with the right catalyst.
tension_points.bear_case: Trump wants to give diplomacy a chance and Iranian negotiators are in talks in Doha. If the midterms pass with neither strikes nor a deal, the risk premium could gradually unwind. ING also says risk-reward does not favor adding longs at current prices.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If the midterms pass with neither strikes nor a deal, the geopolitical premium may unwind.
